==English==

===Etymology===
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:chekmat|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|chekmat}}, from {{der|en|fro|eschec mat}}, from {{der|en|ar|شَاه مَاتَ}}, from {{der|en|fa-cls|شاه مات|tr=šāh māt|t=the king [is] amazed}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈt͡ʃɛkmeɪt/}}
* {{audio|en|En-us-checkmate.ogg|a=US}}

===Interjection===
{{en-intj}}

# {{lb|en|chess}} {{n-g|Word called out by the [[victor]] when making a move that wins the game}}.
# {{lb|en|by extension}} Said when one has placed a person in a losing situation with no escape.

====Alternative forms====
* {{l|en|check and mate}}

====Synonyms====
* {{sense|chess}} [[mate#Interjection|mate]]

===Noun===
{{wp}}
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{lb|en|chess}} The [[conclusive]] [[victory]] in a game of [[chess]] that [[occur]]s when an [[opponent]]'s [[king]] is [[threaten]]ed with [[unavoidable]] [[capture]].
# {{lb|en|figuratively|by extension}} Any [[losing]] [[situation]] with no [[escape]]; [[utter]] [[defeat]].
